newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa packs bags ahead of planned release.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa packs bags ahead of planned release.

text.p: Mother Teresa, recovering rapidly after heart surgery and pneumonia, started packing her bags on Wednesday soon after doctors said they planned to release her later this week.
"Nothing doing. I'm going," A.K. Chatterjee, administrator of Calcutta's Birla Heart Research Centre, quoted a determined Mother Teresa as saying when told she should wait a while.
But the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun eventually agreed to stay on after doctors used their best bed-side manner.
"We had to do a lot of persuasion to convince her that she had to stay on till the doctors officially allowed her to go," Chatterjee told reporters.
"She is getting anxious to go," Dr Patricia Aubanel, a member of the panel treating Mother Teresa, was quoted as saying in a regular medical update on her condition.
"Now she is feeling stronger. If she continues to be stable for another 24 hours, we will consider her discharge to go home soon, so that she continues her recovery there," Aubanel added.
Throughout her stay in hospital, the revered missionary has regularly begged her doctors to let her get back to her work with the poor and the dying.
Mother Teresa, fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had surgery last month to unblock two coronary arteries, the third such operation in five years.
But an irregular heartbeat and long-standing lung and kidney problems delayed her recovery. Twice in the past week doctors have given her a mild electric shock to regulate her heartbeat.
"Mother Teresa's cardiovascular and respiratory status remains stable. Her pneumonia has cleared up," the bulletin said.
Earlier on Wednesday, doctors said they hoped to release the Albanian-born nun later this week, probably on Friday.
"We may release her in a day or two," Dr Tarun Praharaj, another member of the panel, told Reuters.
"That will depend on her progress. She is stable," he added. "We are observing her."
"Mother was very happy to hear this morning that she may be going home soon," an earlier bulletin said. She has been in hospital with heart trouble since November 22.
"The poor people need us so much," it quoted Mother Teresa as saying in response to the news.
Mother Teresa is revered by thousands of people all over the world as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work of compassion and mercy with the downtrodden.

The 1979 Nobel peace prize winner's doctors have said they hope she will be well enough to celebrate Christmas with her colleagues in the order, but have warned that her recovery will be slow and she may never be as active as before.
